monsters.name: Fluffy Bunny
monsters.lore: Meadow bunnies nibble clover all day and thump their feet when strangers come close. Most adventurers' very first fight, and first friend.

monsters.name: Jelly Puff
monsters.lore: A wobbly drop of spring water that learned to bounce. Jelly Puffs gather near ponds and burst into giggles of bubbles when hit.

monsters.name: Pineapple Sprout
monsters.lore: A pineapple top that grew legs and a temper. It hides among the shore bushes and fires needles at anyone after its fruit.

monsters.name: Bouncy Bun
monsters.lore: Soft, round and stubborn as a stone, Bouncy Buns roll down the forest paths of Twilight Woods and flatten whatever's in the way.

monsters.name: Sakura Bunny
monsters.lore: Said to be born where cherry petals fall on a sleeping bunny. Its fur smells of spring and its nibble is strangely bright.

monsters.name: Frost Puff
monsters.lore: A Jelly Puff that slept through a cold night and woke up chilled to the core. Touching it leaves frost on your gloves.

monsters.name: Ember Puff
monsters.lore: A Jelly Puff warmed by swamp gas until it glowed. Keep it away from your hair.

monsters.name: Shade Puff
monsters.lore: A Jelly Puff that soaked up the gloom of the deep woods. It only comes out where the sunlight can't reach.

monsters.name: Dragonfruit Sprout
monsters.lore: A rare cousin of the Pineapple Sprout with a hot pink peel. Its needles sting like sparks.

monsters.name: Cotton Bun
monsters.lore: A Bouncy Bun as light as a cloud. Children in Meadowbrook wish on them for sweet dreams.

monsters.name: Night Bun
monsters.lore: A Bouncy Bun dark as midnight. It bounces silently, and you only notice it when it lands on you.

monsters.name: Golden Hamster
monsters.lore: Stuffs its cheeks with anything shiny, coins included. Beat one and you might get some of your gold back.

monsters.name: Azure Golden Hamster
monsters.lore: A sky-blue Golden Hamster. Collectors pay well just to see one.

monsters.name: Yellow Butterfly
monsters.lore: Meadow butterflies whose wings flash like little mirrors in the sun. The flash is pretty, and blinding.

monsters.name: Crimson Yellow Butterfly
monsters.lore: A Yellow Butterfly with wings like red silk. Spotting one is said to bring a lucky day.

monsters.name: Hedgehog
monsters.lore: A grumpy little digger that flings mud at anyone who steps on its tunnels. Its spines are softer than they look.

monsters.name: Starry Hedgehog
monsters.lore: A Hedgehog with spines that twinkle like a night sky. Nobody knows where it gets the stars.

monsters.name: Wood Crab
monsters.lore: A crab whose shell is bark, scuttling between driftwood on Pineapple Shore. It lashes out with vines it keeps tucked in its claws.

monsters.name: Rosy Wood Crab
monsters.lore: A Wood Crab with rose-coloured bark. It blushes deeper when angry.

monsters.name: Mud Eagle
monsters.lore: Nests in the muddy cliffs along the shore and dives on travellers with a gust of wet wind.

monsters.name: Frosted Mud Eagle
monsters.lore: A Mud Eagle with frost-white feathers, said to nest only on the coldest cliffs.

monsters.name: Wood Monkey
monsters.lore: Cheeky monkeys of the Smiling Forest. They steal apples, hats and anything that isn't tied down.

monsters.name: Shadow Wood Monkey
monsters.lore: A Wood Monkey with dark fur that hides in the canopy. You'll hear its laugh before you see it.

monsters.name: Tree Snake
monsters.lore: Hangs from branches pretending to be a vine until something walks underneath.

monsters.name: Sunny Tree Snake
monsters.lore: A Tree Snake with golden scales that likes to bask in the sun spots of the forest.

monsters.name: Flame Sheep
monsters.lore: Its wool is always smouldering. Shearing one is a job for the brave, or the fireproof.

monsters.name: Mint Flame Sheep
monsters.lore: A Flame Sheep with cool mint-green wool. Its fire smells oddly fresh.

monsters.name: Wood Hog
monsters.lore: A tusked boar that roots through the forest floor. Its roar can be heard across the Smiling Forest.

monsters.name: Violet Wood Hog
monsters.lore: A Wood Hog with purple bristles. Rarer, and even grumpier.

monsters.name: Werewolf
monsters.lore: Prowls Twilight Woods when the moon is up. Its bite carries a shadow that saps your strength.

monsters.name: Amber Werewolf
monsters.lore: A Werewolf with amber fur that glows faintly in moonlight.

monsters.name: Dark Beetle
monsters.lore: A shiny black beetle that thrives in caves and dark places. Its jaws are sharper than its manners.

monsters.name: Azure Dark Beetle
monsters.lore: A Dark Beetle with a blue sheen, found in the deepest caves.

monsters.name: Treefrog
monsters.lore: The croakers of Frog Swamp. They sing all night long and keep the whole region awake.

monsters.name: Crimson Treefrog
monsters.lore: A bright red Treefrog. The colour is a warning: it's tougher than it looks.

monsters.name: Blue Treefrog
monsters.lore: A Treefrog that took to the water. It spits bubbles instead of using vines.

monsters.name: Golden Treefrog
monsters.lore: A Treefrog with metallic gold skin. Swamp folk say it's the frogs' king in disguise.

monsters.name: Water Slug
monsters.lore: A slow, friendly slug that leaves a trail of fresh water. Calm until you poke it.

monsters.name: Starry Water Slug
monsters.lore: A Water Slug speckled with glowing dots, like a little piece of the night sky.

monsters.name: Wisp
monsters.lore: Floating lights that drift through Shiverdell. Some say they're lost souls; others say they're just shy.

monsters.name: Rosy Wisp
monsters.lore: A Wisp with a soft pink glow. Its flash is gentle but dazzling.

monsters.name: Earth Lion
monsters.lore: King of the open plains, with a mane caked in dust. Its roar shakes the ground.

monsters.name: Frosted Earth Lion
monsters.lore: An Earth Lion with a frost-white mane. Its roar leaves a chill in the air.

monsters.name: Blaze Bull
monsters.lore: Charges at anything red, and everything else too. Its horns are hot to the touch.

monsters.name: Shadow Blaze Bull
monsters.lore: A Blaze Bull with a coat as dark as soot. It charges without warning.

monsters.name: Fire Rat
monsters.lore: Lives in the warm tunnels of Rat Cavern and sets fire to anything it chews.

monsters.name: Sunny Fire Rat
monsters.lore: A Fire Rat with bright yellow fur that glows like a lantern in the dark tunnels.

monsters.name: Black Widow
monsters.lore: A desert spider that spins sticky webs across the dunes. Its bite is shadowy and cold.

monsters.name: Mint Black Widow
monsters.lore: A Black Widow with mint-green markings. Just as dangerous, but prettier.

quests.name: The Waystone in the Tall Grass

monsters.name: Black Lizard
monsters.lore: Basks on the hot desert rocks by day and hunts in the shade at dusk.

monsters.name: Violet Black Lizard
monsters.lore: A Black Lizard with violet scales, rarely seen above ground.

monsters.name: Floating Stone
monsters.lore: A rock that forgot how to fall. Crystal Mountain is full of them, and they throw pebbles at climbers.

monsters.name: Amber Floating Stone
monsters.lore: A Floating Stone of warm amber. Something tiny seems to be trapped inside.

monsters.name: Golden Cloud
monsters.lore: A cloud of gold dust that spins and flashes. Miners follow them hoping to find treasure.

monsters.name: Azure Golden Cloud
monsters.lore: A Golden Cloud with a blue tint, said to rain silver coins once a year.

monsters.name: Gem Crawler
monsters.lore: A beetle encrusted with crystals that shine when it moves. Its flash lights up whole caverns.

monsters.name: Crimson Gem Crawler
monsters.lore: A Gem Crawler covered in ruby-red crystals. Jewellers dream of finding one.

monsters.name: Fire Bear
monsters.lore: A bear with fur like embers that roams the rocky mountainsides, warming the stones wherever it walks.

monsters.name: Starry Fire Bear
monsters.lore: A Fire Bear whose fur sparkles with tiny stars. It glows warmly among the rocks.

monsters.name: Pegasus
monsters.lore: A winged horse that soars above Snow White Forest. It rarely lands, and only for the worthy.

monsters.name: Rosy Pegasus
monsters.lore: A Pegasus with rose-pink wings. Seeing one is considered a blessing.

monsters.name: Phantom
monsters.lore: A cold spirit that floats through snowy woods and sleepy streets, whispering in your ear.

monsters.name: Frosted Phantom
monsters.lore: A Phantom frozen into icy blue, haunting the shores of Briarmere.

monsters.name: Snowman
monsters.lore: Someone built it, and then it walked away. Its frost breath chills to the bone.

monsters.name: Shadow Snowman
monsters.lore: A Snowman made of grey, dirty snow. It's not friendly about it.

monsters.name: Poison Skeleton
monsters.lore: Old bones held together by a nasty magic. It throws webs and bites with a poisonous grin.

monsters.name: Sunny Poison Skeleton
monsters.lore: A Poison Skeleton with sun-bleached golden bones. Strangely cheerful for a skeleton.

monsters.name: Shadow Ape
monsters.lore: A huge dark ape that guards the paths near Moonwhisper. It throws boulders like pebbles.

monsters.name: Mint Shadow Ape
monsters.lore: A Shadow Ape with mint-green fur. Even bigger, if that's possible.

monsters.name: Red Butterfly
monsters.lore: A butterfly with fiery wings. Where it flutters, little embers fall.

monsters.name: Night Monkey
monsters.lore: A Wood Monkey's cousin that only comes out after dark, with a bite full of shadow.

monsters.name: Mud Slime
monsters.lore: A Jelly Puff that rolled in the mud and never washed. Squelchy and surprisingly heavy.

monsters.name: Fire Crab
monsters.lore: A crab with a red-hot shell. Fishermen use it to cook their lunch, carefully.

monsters.name: Black Bull
monsters.lore: A Blaze Bull's darker cousin. Its eyes glow in the night, and its charge is just as hard.

monsters.name: Light Mouse
monsters.lore: A tiny mouse that glows softly. It lights the way for lost travellers in Shiverdell.

monsters.name: Earth Snake
monsters.lore: Burrows through the cavern floor and pops up to spit mud at your boots.

monsters.name: Light Snake
monsters.lore: A snake whose scales shine like polished glass in the desert sun.

monsters.name: Light Hedgehog
monsters.lore: A Hedgehog whose spines glow like little candles in the desert night.

monsters.name: Mining Lizard
monsters.lore: A lizard that digs for ore in the mountains and throws rocks at anyone near its find.

monsters.name: Frost Bear
monsters.lore: A Fire Bear's icy cousin, white as fresh snow, with a breath that freezes the air.

monsters.name: Rat King
monsters.lore: The boss of Rat Cavern: a fat, crowned rat that rules its tunnels with fire and fury.

bossAt.greeting: Squeak! Who dares enter MY cavern? Bow to the king!

victory.title: The Rat King Falls
story: The Rat King's crown rolls across the cavern floor and spins to a stop. The rats look at it, look at each other, and scatter.
With no king in the way, the dwarves of Ingothold aren't cut off anymore. Tell Elder Oak: the road south through Shiverdell can open at last.

monsters.name: Drunk Dragon
monsters.lore: A dragon who drank too much at the desert oasis. Wobbly, loud, and still very much a dragon.

bossAt.greeting: *hic* Heyyy… you wanna piece of this? *hic*

victory.title: A Dragon Sobers Up
story: The Drunk Dragon hiccups out one last puff of smoke, lies down by the oasis and starts to snore. It's going to wake up with a terrible headache.
The caravans can come back to the oasis, and Ingothold's trade with them. Chief Brom will want to hear, and with the desert safe, the roads out of Ingothold can open.

monsters.name: Big Bad Wolf
monsters.lore: The wolf of the old stories. It prowls Snow White Forest looking for anyone in a red hood.

bossAt.greeting: Grrr… what big eyes you have. All the better to FIGHT you with!

victory.title: Nobody's Afraid Anymore
story: The Big Bad Wolf huffs, puffs and runs off into the snow with its tail between its legs. It won't be blowing any houses down.
Red hoods can walk Snow White Forest without looking over their shoulders. Mayor Poppy will want to hear, and Prismhaven is buzzing with news from Moonwhisper.

quests.name: Who's Afraid of the Big Bad Wolf?

monsters.name: Golden Slime
monsters.lore: A slime made of molten gold. Adventurers hunt it for riches; it doesn't appreciate that.

monsters.name: Candy Puff
monsters.lore: A Jelly Puff made of sugar. It tastes as sweet as it looks, but don't try.

monsters.name: Temple Jelly
monsters.lore: Sacred jellies that guard the Tidewater Shrine, blessed by its ancient springs.

monsters.name: Earth Wolf
monsters.lore: A sandy-brown wolf that hunts in packs on the mountain trails.

monsters.name: Flame Wolf
monsters.lore: A wolf with a burning mane, part of the pack in Big Bad Wolf's Lair.

monsters.name: Wooden Puppet
monsters.lore: A carved puppet brought to life by a strange magic on Marionette Rise. It still dances when nobody's looking.

monsters.name: Lotus Sprite
monsters.lore: A tiny spirit born from a lotus flower. It blesses the ponds of Lotus Land.

monsters.name: Dream Phantom
monsters.lore: A phantom that lives in the dreams of Dozywick's residents, and won't let them wake.

monsters.name: Dreamstone Golem
monsters.lore: A golem made of dreamstone, built to guard the riches of Ingothold. It never stops working.

monsters.name: Crystal Widow
monsters.lore: A spider made of living crystal, spinning glittering webs in the Whispering Hollow.

monsters.name: Emerald Pegasus
monsters.lore: A green-winged Pegasus that guards the Emerald Road, shining like a jewel.

monsters.name: Gilded Brute
monsters.lore: A servant of the Gilded King, guarding the depths of Gooey Grotto with fire and roars.

bossAt.greeting: The Gilded King's treasure is mine! Mine, mine, MINE!

victory.title: Fool's Gold
story: The Brute topples back into its hoard, and the hoard goes clink. Pebbles. Painted gold, every last one.
If the Gilded King was ever here, it left long ago. With no one to shout at them, the Golden Slimes go back to bouncing, and Elder Oak will have a good laugh.

monsters.name: Howlmaster
monsters.lore: The leader of the wolf pack, scarred and wise. Every wolf in the lair answers to it.

bossAt.greeting: Grrr... the sheep's lambs are ours. Turn back, little hero.

victory.title: The Lambs Come Home
story: The Howlmaster limps off into the dark, and the pack slinks after it. Behind a rock, something small says baa.
Mother Sheep's lambs are free, and they know the way home over Gumdrop Peaks. Nella the Tailor will be glad: no wool is finer than a happy lamb's.

monsters.name: Marionette King
monsters.lore: The master of Marionette Rise, who pulls the strings of every puppet there.

bossAt.greeting: Dance! Dance for your king, forever and ever!

victory.title: The Strings Are Cut
story: The Marionette King's strings go slack. All over the hill the puppets stop mid-step and sit down, as if someone finally told them they could rest.
Hermit Orrin says they used to dance for children. Maybe one day they will again, but only when they want to. The animals can come home to Marionette Rise.

monsters.name: Craghulk
monsters.lore: A mountain of rock that snores in the cave by Dozywick. Its snoring has kept the whole town dreaming for a year.

victory.title: Dozywick Wakes Up
story: The Craghulk crumbles into a heap of quiet stones. The snoring that filled the cave for a whole year stops.
In town, someone yawns, then someone else. For the first time in a year, Rosalind's eyes open, and Jory has a whole year of news to tell.

monsters.name: Morvane
monsters.lore: A dark lord of legend who waits on the Hidden Steppe. Few who face it come back to tell the tale.

bossAt.greeting: The goddess's treasure has a guardian, and it is me.

victory.title: The Goddess's Treasure
story: Morvane sinks to one knee. “Then guard it well,” it rumbles, and fades into the grass like a shadow at noon.
Where it stood, Dreamstone glows in the earth, bright as a golem's heart. Ambrose the Wise will want to hear, but the ore's trail runs on, south to Sneezle Sands.

monsters.name: Wavecrest Dragon
monsters.lore: The ancient guardian of the Tidewater Shrine, with scales like ocean waves.

bossAt.greeting: The lake keeps its secrets. So will your bones.

victory.title: The Tide Turns
story: The Wavecrest Dragon sinks into the deepest pool of the temple, and the water goes still for the first time in an age.
The Tidewater Shrine still keeps its secrets, but no longer with teeth. The Temple Keeper can walk its halls again, and boats can cross Briarmere without fear.

monsters.name: Silverfang Warden
monsters.lore: A lieutenant of the Silver Wraith, guarding the Whispering Hollow with cold steel.

bossAt.greeting: The Silver Wraith sends his regards.

victory.title: The Way Is Open
story: The Warden's silver armour clatters to the cave floor, empty. Whatever was inside has fled, back to the master it served.
Travellers can pass through the Whispering Hollow to the Emerald Road again. The Emerald Guard will want to hear. And somewhere far away, the Silver Wraith knows your name.

monsters.name: Emerald Dragon
monsters.lore: The legendary dragon at the end of the Emerald Road, the greatest challenge in Dorlune.

bossAt.greeting: At the end of the road, a dragon. Of course there is.

victory.title: The Emerald Gates
story: The Emerald Dragon lowers its great head and steps aside. Behind it, the gates of the Emerald City shine green in the evening light.
From a wooden sword in Meadowbrook to the gates of the Emerald City, you've walked the longest road in Dorlune. The Emerald Guard will hardly believe it.

quests.name: At the End of the Road

monsters.name: Grumpy Old Oak
monsters.lore: An old oak tree that's been grumpy for a thousand years. It hates having its branches climbed.

bossAt.greeting: Hrmph. Stop smiling at me. STOP IT.

victory.title: The Forest Smiles Again
story: The Grumpy Old Oak creaks, sags, and lets out a sigh a thousand years long. Then, slowly, the corners of its bark curl up.
It will never admit it, but it rather likes the Wood Monkeys swinging in its branches. The Smiling Forest lives up to its name again.

monsters.name: Great Wisp
monsters.lore: The mother of all Wisps, a huge glowing light at the heart of Shiverdell.

bossAt.greeting: Ooooh, follow the pretty light... just a little further... hee hee!

victory.title: The Light Goes Out
story: The Great Wisp flickers, giggles one last time and goes out like a candle. All over the valley, the little lights fade with it.
Travellers can keep to the road again; Shiverdell is only a dark valley now. Only the cavern to the east still squeaks.

monsters.name: Moon Rabbit Queen
monsters.lore: The queen of the moon rabbits, who descends on Moonwhisper when the moon is full.

bossAt.greeting: Who stole my moon-mochi? Was it YOU? Hop to it and face me!

victory.title: The Queen Hops Home
story: The Moon Rabbit Queen sits down with a bump, ears drooping. Then a small rabbit peeks out from behind the throne, cheeks full, whiskers dusted with mochi.
Mystery solved. The queen scoops up the little thief and hops back up to the moon, and Moonwhisper can sleep under a quiet full moon again.

monsters.name: Starmoth
monsters.lore: Moths drawn to the fallen star's light. Their wings carry its dust, and they drink the glow from any lantern left out at night.

monsters.name: Dawn Starmoth
monsters.lore: A Starmoth that flew too close to the sunrise. Its wings have blushed pink ever since.

monsters.name: Nebula Puff
monsters.lore: A puff of the night sky that drifted down with the fallen star. It settles on moonflowers and lulls them to sleep.

monsters.name: Crystal Quill
monsters.lore: A hedgehog whose quills turned to crystal where the starlight landed. It digs up crystal gardens for a crunchy snack.

monsters.name: Fallen Star
monsters.lore: The star that fell on Starfall Isle long ago. Awake on its hill, lonely and far from home, it blazes at anyone who comes near.

bossAt.greeting: The light on the hill flares as you come near, humming like a lost song.

victory.title: A Star Goes Home
story: The Fallen Star flickers, then dims to a soft, warm glow. It was never angry, only lonely, and very far from home.
Down in Glimmerbough the lanterns light up one by one. That night the star rises from the hill, slowly, and settles back into its place in the sky, and the wisps drift up after it.

monsters.name: Prism Crab
monsters.lore: A crab whose shell grew into amethyst in the Glimmerdeep's pools. It snips crystals off the walls and wears the prettiest ones.

monsters.name: Floating Geode
monsters.lore: A hollow stone that drifts through the dark with a heart of glimmering crystal. Crack one open and it glows for a hundred years.

monsters.name: Crystal Serpent
monsters.lore: A serpent of living glass that swims through the crystals as if they were water. You only see it by the light it bends.

monsters.name: Prism Drake
monsters.lore: A drake that crept into the Glimmerdeep long ago and fed on the starlight in its crystals until its scales turned to living prism. It sleeps curled round the brightest shard of all.

bossAt.greeting: Light ripples across a coil of crystal scales. Something vast lifts its head, and every crystal in the cave flares at once.

victory.title: The Glimmerdeep Shines
story: The Prism Drake's scales soften from blinding white to a sleepy glow. It was never wicked, only hungry, and starlight is a hard habit to break.
It curls up round its shard and drifts off to sleep, and the light it drank seeps back up through the crystals. That night every lantern in Glimmerbough burns a little brighter.

monsters.name: Comet Hare
monsters.lore: A hare that hops so fast across the isle's meadows that it leaves a tail of starlight behind it. The fairies say a fallen star taught it to run.

monsters.name: Dusk Comet Hare
monsters.lore: A Comet Hare that only runs at sunset. Its tail glows gold instead of blue, and it's gone before you can blink.

monsters.name: Lantern Sprite
monsters.lore: A moth-winged sprite that carries a lantern lit from the fallen star. It leads lost travellers home, or deeper into the woods if it's feeling cheeky.

monsters.name: Moonlamp Sprite
monsters.lore: A Lantern Sprite whose flame burns cold and blue. It only comes out on moonless nights, to stand in for the moon.

monsters.name: Shardwing Bat
monsters.lore: A bat whose wings grew crystal in the Glimmerdeep's dark. It hangs from the ceiling in rows, chiming softly when it shivers.

monsters.name: Rosequartz Bat
monsters.lore: Shardwing Bats from the Depths, where the crystal blushes pink. They're bigger and bolder than their cousins up top.

monsters.name: Gloomwing Bat
monsters.lore: Down by the Glimmerdeep's heart, where no light has ever reached, the bats' crystal wings have gone as dark as the night sky.

monsters.name: Geode Golem
monsters.lore: A little golem made of cave rock, with amethyst growing out of its back. It collects pretty stones and gets very upset if you take one.

monsters.name: Sapphire Golem
monsters.lore: A Geode Golem from the Depths, its crystals blue as deep water. It sits so still that miners have built shelves on it.

monsters.name: Heartstone Golem
monsters.lore: The oldest golems keep watch at the Glimmerdeep's heart, their crystals glowing red as embers. They say the Prism Drake raised them.

monsters.name: Frost Skeleton
monsters.lore: A Poison Skeleton that wandered too far north. Frost creeps through its bones, and its bite numbs.

monsters.name: Ember Skeleton
monsters.lore: Bones baked by the desert sun until they smoulder. It leaves little scorch marks wherever it hops.

monsters.name: Grave Skeleton
monsters.lore: A Poison Skeleton from the oldest graves, its bones tinged violet by an old curse. The curse lingers long after it's gone.

monsters.name: Crimson Skeleton
monsters.lore: A Poison Skeleton with bones gone black as soot and a red glow where its eyes should be. Even the bravest bulls give it room.

monsters.name: Snow Treefrog
monsters.lore: A Treefrog as white as fresh snow, headband and all. It trains in the cold to toughen up.

monsters.name: Shadow Treefrog
monsters.lore: A Treefrog that only trains at night. You'll hear its battle croak long before you see it.

monsters.name: Midnight Pegasus
monsters.lore: A Pegasus with a mane like the night sky. It only flies when the stars are out.

monsters.name: Frost Pineapple Sprout
monsters.lore: A Pineapple Sprout that napped in the snow and woke up frozen. Still sweet, just very cold.

monsters.name: Mossy Hedgehog
monsters.lore: A Hedgehog that sat still so long that moss grew on its spines. It doesn't seem to mind.

monsters.name: Ember Bun
monsters.lore: A Bun that bounced too close to a campfire and never cooled down. Mind your fingers.

people.name: Elder Oak
people.greeting: Ah, a new face! Meadowbrook could use a helping hand.

services.name: Nurse Mira
services.greeting: Tired, dear? Rest here and your whole party will feel brand new.

services.name: Barber Wick
services.greeting: A trim, a curl or a whole new colour? Sit yourself down and I'll have you looking like a hero in no time.

services.name: Banker Penny
services.greeting: Coins, gear, keepsakes: whatever you leave with me stays safe, whatever befalls you out there.

services.name: Trader Bo
services.greeting: Potions, blades, robes — take a look!

services.name: Captain Brann
services.greeting: The Warrior Guild wants strong arms and brave hearts.

services.name: Sage Lumi
services.greeting: The Arcane Circle studies the seven elements. Magic is a path of patience.

services.name: Ranger Pip
services.greeting: The Wildfolk Lodge! We befriend beasts, not beat them. Well, mostly.

services.name: Smith Tobin
services.greeting: Clang! Bring me wood and metal from the wilds and I'll forge you something fine.

services.name: Orla the Weaver
services.greeting: Every cape I weave tells a story. Beat every monster in a land and I'll weave you its colours; do greater things, and I'll weave you greater capes.

locals.name: Little Lou
lines: I'm going to be an adventurer when I grow up!
Elder Oak says I need a sword. I've got a stick. Same thing.
Tess's brother went off adventuring. He isn't back yet.
When I'm big I'll go and find him. Unless you find him first!

people.name: Mother Sheep
people.greeting: Baa! Oh, a kind face at last.

people.name: Miller Rosie
people.greeting: Welcome to Cloverdale! Mind the flour. It gets everywhere, even in the bread.

people.name: Beekeeper Barnaby
people.greeting: Shh. Slow movements, please. The bees are watching, and so am I.

locals.name: Old Fisher Gil
lines: Shh... they're biting today.
I've fished this lake since I was knee-high to a jelly.
Caught one THIS big once. Well... this big. Fine, a tadpole.
Come back at sunset. The whole lake turns gold.

locals.name: Tess
lines: My brother Wil crossed this bridge to see the world.
He said he'd be back before the blossoms fell.
The blossoms have fallen twice now.
He went east, to the dark woods. He's scared of the dark, you know.
If you meet a boy with a wooden sword, tell him Tess is waiting.

locals.name: Farmer Hollis
lines: Jelly Puffs ate my cabbages again!
I put up a scarecrow. They bounced on it.
Elder Oak says an adventurer will sort them out.
Is that you? You look like an adventurer. Mostly.

locals.name: Granny Maple
lines: This well's older than I am, and I'm older than most of the hills.
Rosie's mother ran the mill before her, and her mother before that.
When the clover blooms, the whole of Cloverdale smells of honey.
Mind the Jelly Puffs on your way. They don't bite, but they do wobble.

locals.name: Farmhand Jem
lines: Rosie mills the flour, Barnaby keeps the bees, and I eat the honey bread.
The hamsters only raid the granary when nobody's looking. So, always.
Barnaby talks to his bees. He says they talk back. I've never heard it.
Best bread between here and Meadowbrook. Don't tell Meadowbrook.

locals.name: Farmer Bram
lines: Mind the pumpkins! They bruise if you look at them wrong.
The scarecrow does his best. The crows aren't impressed.
Rain, sun, slimes in the cabbages. A farmer's work is never done.

people.name: Old Shelly
people.greeting: Click-clack! Mind the tide pools, youngster.

people.name: Fishwife Marla
people.greeting: Fresh fish! Well, it was fresh this morning, before the Mud Eagles got to it.

people.name: Net-Mender Oskar
people.greeting: Every knot I tie, a crab snips. Every knot!

locals.name: Beachcomber Nell
lines: Every tide brings something new. Yesterday, a boot.
Today, the other boot!
Old Shelly says the Mud Eagles snatch all the pretty shells.
I found a bottle with a message once. It said 'Hello'. So I wrote back.

locals.name: Captain Salt
lines: Forty years at sea, and I never saw a pineapple swim.
Then I came here. They don't swim. They hop.
Some say a ship sank off this shore, full of gold.
I say it was full of pineapples. Look around you.

locals.name: Little Coral
lines: This sandcastle is for the Wood Crabs, so they leave Oskar's nets alone.
Mum says the lamp on the point went out in the storm. Now the boats get lost.
Captain Salt says he sailed past the edge of the map once. I believe him.
Nell finds the best shells. I find the best crabs. They find my toes.

locals.name: Bosun Ike
lines: Driftwood Cove's built from whatever the sea throws up. Mostly driftwood.
The Salty Gull has the best fish stew on the shore. It's the only one.
Mud Eagles can spot a herring from the clouds. Clever birds. Rude, though.
No light on the point, no boats in at night. It's as simple as that.

locals.name: Wanderer Pell
lines: Pull up a log. The fire's warm and the stew is nearly edible.
I've slept under every sky in Dorlune. This one's my favourite.
Travel light, friend, and never camp downwind of a jelly.

people.name: Willow the Wisp
people.greeting: Shh... the woods are listening.

people.name: Lampwright Fenwick
people.greeting: In Duskhollow it's always nearly night. Good for lanterns. Bad for reading.

people.name: Charcoal-Burner Hettie
people.greeting: Soot on your boots? Then you've found Duskhollow.

locals.name: Wil
lines: I'm not lost. I'm exploring.
...Okay, I'm a little lost.
Did my sister send you? Tess worries too much.
The wisps keep showing me the way out, then giggling.
Tell Tess I'll be home soon. Right after I find the way.

locals.name: Granny Thistle
lines: Glow-caps for a sleeping draught. Sparkle-ferns for a waking one.
Never mix them up. Ask Dozywick how that went.
Willow the Wisp fades a little more each night.
The Shade Puffs drink the moonlight, poor dear.

locals.name: Lantern Girl Ivy
lines: I light every lantern in Duskhollow, every evening. It's always evening.
Fenwick makes lantern glass from beetle shells. Don't tell the beetles.
The Night Market is the best night of the month. It's also every night.
Howling at night? Only the Werewolves. Nothing to worry about. Probably.

locals.name: Moth-Catcher Silas
lines: I catch moths and let them go again. It's a hobby, not a living.
Hettie's charcoal burns so slow you could cook a stew all week on it.
Willow the Wisp drifts by now and then. We wave. It flickers.
A Night Monkey took my best net last market. Bold as you like.

locals.name: Wanderer Isa
lines: Pull up a log. The fire's warm and the stew is nearly edible.
I've slept under every sky in Dorlune. This one's my favourite.
Travel light, friend, and never camp downwind of a jelly.

people.name: Little Pig
people.greeting: Oink! Have you seen a wolf around here?

people.name: Orchard-Keeper Moss
people.greeting: Hollyhock's apples are the sweetest in the forest. Ask the monkeys. They'd know.

people.name: Cooper Beatrix
people.greeting: Barrels! Kegs! Tubs! If it holds cider, I made it.

locals.name: Woodcutter Bram
lines: I'd never cut a tree that smiles. Only the grumpy ones.
There's just the one grumpy one. And I'm not cutting HIM.
He swatted my hat clean off last spring.
Little Pig asked me for sticks. I told him: bricks!

locals.name: Shepherd Lark
lines: Easy, Ember. No setting the nice adventurer on fire.
Flame Sheep make the warmest wool. If you can catch them.
Prismhaven's mayor wants them kept away from the market awnings.
Ember only sets fire to things she loves. So... everything.

locals.name: Odile the Mapmaker
lines: Mapping the river. It keeps moving.
Rivers don't move? Tell that to this one.
Every land is a page of Liora's book, you know. I'm drawing them all.
This is page... twelve? I've lost count of the pages.

locals.name: Cider-Taster Gus
lines: Tasting cider is hard work. Somebody has to do it, and it's me.
Beatrix's truffle cider tastes like mushrooms and regret. I love it.
The Apple Fair is next week, if the Flame Sheep leave us any apples.
Woodcutter Bram brings the wood for Beatrix's barrels. Good man.

locals.name: Little Posy
lines: I'm guarding the apples. From monkeys. And from Gus.
Moss says every tree in the orchard has a name. That one's Gertrude.
A Wood Monkey threw an apple at me! It was a good apple, though.
When I win the Apple Fair I'll get a ribbon as big as my head.

locals.name: Farmer Odette
lines: Mind the pumpkins! They bruise if you look at them wrong.
The scarecrow does his best. The crows aren't impressed.
Rain, sun, slimes in the cabbages. A farmer's work is never done.

people.name: Mayor Poppy
people.greeting: Oh! You came all the way through the Smiling Forest? Splendid!

quests.name: Who's Afraid of the Big Bad Wolf?

people.name: Tilly the Toymaker
people.greeting: Oh, hello! I make a toy of every monster I've seen a card of. Found any cards on your travels?

services.name: Healer Lily
services.greeting: Welcome to Prismhaven! Rest a while, adventurer.

services.name: Barber Juno
services.greeting: Every colour of the rainbow, right here in Prismhaven! Which one will your hair be today?

services.name: Banker Opal
services.greeting: Prismhaven's vaults have never lost a coin. Leave what you don't need to carry with me.

services.name: Prismhaven Market
services.greeting: The finest goods this side of the rainbow!

services.name: Smith Iris
services.greeting: Monsters drop the best materials. Bring them here and we'll make something sharp.

locals.name: Painter Ivo
lines: I'm painting Prismhaven. I've run out of colours.
There are more colours here than in my whole box.
Tilly the Toymaker wants me to paint her toys. All of them.
Have you seen the fountain at night? Every colour at once.

people.name: Mister Frost
people.greeting: Brrr-illiant to see you!

people.name: Foreman Barrowby
people.greeting: Seven dwarfs, seven hearths, one very small kitchen.

people.name: Housekeeper Blanche
people.greeting: Seven dwarfs, seven pairs of muddy boots, and one of me. Wipe your feet!

locals.name: Granny Edda
lines: Soup for Mister Frost. Cold soup, he insists.
He's a dear, but he won't come down. Says it's too warm.
Mind the wolf on the way up. He's all teeth and manners.
There's a chest up at the top too. Nobody knows who left it.

locals.name: Dwarf Fennick
lines: Seven of us, there were. Now it's just me and six snowmen.
The others went down to Ingothold for the winter.
I stayed for the apples. Have you tried them? Not the shiny ones.
A princess kept house for us once. She's off being royal now.

locals.name: Dwarf Grimbly
lines: Off to the mine, back from the mine. That's the whole song.
Blanche makes us wash before supper. All seven of us. It takes a while.
The Frost Bears like our woodpile. They like it frozen solid.
Mister Frost up on the hill sends his regards. And a lot of snow.

locals.name: Dwarf Hobb
lines: I built this snowman. He's the eighth dwarf. Don't tell the others.
Seven hearths means seven fires. Lovely and warm, in the middle.
Granny Edda says Blanche turned up one winter and just stayed. Good thing too.
Frost Apples are sweet as honey, if you can get them off a Snowman.

locals.name: Wanderer Pell
lines: Pull up a log. The fire's warm and the stew is nearly edible.
I've slept under every sky in Dorlune. This one's my favourite.
Travel light, friend, and never camp downwind of a jelly.

requires.name: Who's Afraid of the Big Bad Wolf?

people.name: Frog Prince
people.greeting: Ribbit. I am a prince, you know. Truly.

people.name: Ugly Duckling
people.greeting: Oh... hello. You don't think I'm ugly, do you?

people.name: Eel-Catcher Ida
people.greeting: Eels? No eels today. Only frogs. It's always frogs.

people.name: Herbalist Mungo
people.greeting: Mind where you step. Half of Bogbottom is medicine and the other half is mud.

locals.name: Old Reed
lines: Ribbit. Sorry. Live here long enough, it slips out.
The Frog Prince says he's a real prince. They all say that.
He lost his golden ball in the pond. The Water Slugs sit on it like eggs.
The frogs sing all night. Meadowbrook complains. I sleep like a log.

locals.name: Duck-Keeper Maud
lines: That little grey duckling? Don't you listen to the Mud Slimes.
Every swan was a duckling once. Every single one.
One day it'll fly north to Swan Lake. You'll see.

locals.name: Stilt-Walker Nib
lines: In Bogbottom everyone walks on stilts. Except when they fall off.
Mungo's mud cures everything. Colds, scrapes, wobbly knees.
The Blue Treefrogs croak under the boardwalk all night. Ribbit, ribbit.
Duck-Keeper Maud says her ducks don't like the slugs either.

locals.name: Old Croaker Bess
lines: They call me Old Croaker. I sing to the frogs. They don't sing back.
Ida's chased the Great Eel for forty years. It's chased her for forty-one.
Slugs on the stilts again. Everything's slippery. My knees can't take it.
Mud's good for you. Mungo says so, and he's a hundred and three.

locals.name: Wanderer Isa
lines: Pull up a log. The fire's warm and the stew is nearly edible.
I've slept under every sky in Dorlune. This one's my favourite.
Travel light, friend, and never camp downwind of a jelly.

people.name: Brave Mouse
people.greeting: Squeak! Small, but brave!

people.name: Chandler Mabbott
people.greeting: Candles! Tall ones, short ones, and ones that don't blow out when a Wisp says boo.

people.name: Bell-Ringer Prue
people.greeting: Every hour I ring the bell, so the whole valley knows it isn't alone.

locals.name: Lamplighter Ansel
lines: Keep to the road, friend. The lights off it aren't mine.
I light these lanterns every night. The Great Wisp blows them out.
Travellers follow its pretty light and never come back.
Well. They come back. Very muddy and very embarrassed.

locals.name: Dwarf Tolly
lines: The cavern's ours. Was ours. The rats have it now.
A Rat King, if you please! With a crown and everything.
Ingothold is cut off till someone sorts him out.
Bring a light. And cheese. Rats love cheese.

locals.name: Nervous Norbert
lines: Did you hear that? No? Good. Neither did I. Probably.
I moved to Candlewick because it's got the most candles. Dark's not for me.
Ansel lights the lamps on the road. I follow him home every night.
When the bell went quiet, I didn't sleep for a week. Still haven't, really.

locals.name: Brave Little Hester
lines: I'm not scared of Wisps. They're just lights with opinions.
The Brave Mouse is my hero. He stood up to a Blaze Bull!
Mabbott lets me dip the candles. I've made twelve. Eleven are lumpy.
When I grow up I'll ring the bell, louder than Prue even.

locals.name: Wanderer Pell
lines: Pull up a log. The fire's warm and the stew is nearly edible.
I've slept under every sky in Dorlune. This one's my favourite.
Travel light, friend, and never camp downwind of a jelly.

people.name: Ratcatcher Bodkin
people.greeting: Rats! Rats everywhere! Good for business, bad for my nerves.

locals.name: Scout Hode
lines: Ingothold sent me to scout. I've scouted. It's rats.
Big rats. And a king rat, with a crown made of spoons.
Our spoons! From Ingothold!
Sort him out and we'll make you a new set. Of spoons.

locals.name: Apprentice Squeak
lines: Bodkin calls me Squeak because I squeak when I see a rat. I see a lot of rats.
The Rat King's down there somewhere. We don't go that far.
Scout Hode maps the tunnels. I map where I've been bitten.
One day I'll catch a Fire Rat with my bare hands. With gloves on.

people.name: Chief Brom
people.greeting: You cleared the cavern? Then Ingothold owes you one, friend.

services.name: Healer Brunhild
services.greeting: Hammer-bruised? Sit down, I'll patch you up.

services.name: Barber Thorne
services.greeting: Even a dwarf needs a good cut now and then. I'll leave your beard be, unless you want it dyed to match.

services.name: Banker Gunnar
services.greeting: Dwarven vaults, carved in solid rock. Your gold won't be safer anywhere in the world.

services.name: Dwarven Forge
services.greeting: Forged in Ingothold, built to last a thousand years!

services.name: Smith Ingot
services.greeting: Ingothold steel is the finest there is. Show me what you've gathered.

locals.name: Old Miner Dunmore
lines: Ingothold steel! Best in the world. Ask anyone. Ask me.
We were cut off for a year when the Rat King took the cavern.
Then someone sorted him out. Was that you? Have a nod, then.
Crystal Mountain's south of here. Gem Crawlers. Good shells.

people.name: Puss in Boots
people.greeting: Good day! A fine pair of boots you have.

people.name: Lamp-Seller Kasim
people.greeting: Lamps! Old lamps, new lamps, lamps with a genie in, lamps without. Mostly without.

people.name: Well-Keeper Samira
people.greeting: In the desert, a well is worth more than gold. Ask anyone who's been thirsty.

locals.name: Caravan Master Zara
lines: The caravans wait. There's a dragon in the oasis.
A drunk dragon. Singing. Badly.
We used to rest there. Now we rest here and complain.
Sober him up and the first figs are yours.

locals.name: Odile the Mapmaker
lines: The sand moves every night. My map of here is mostly guesses.
I drew a dune. By morning it was a different dune.
Somewhere out here, a lamp holds a genie. Or a very cramped lizard.
This page of Liora's book is the hardest to draw.

locals.name: Carpet-Weaver Layla
lines: My carpets don't fly. Well, one did once, but it came back.
Kasim sells a hundred lamps and swears one of them has a genie.
Zara's caravans stop here for water, and for gossip.
A cat in boots came through last week. Very polite. Took nothing.

locals.name: Storyteller Hakim
lines: Sit, sit. I know a thousand stories and one more besides.
Once a boy found a lamp in a cave, and rubbed it. You know the rest.
The well here never runs dry. Samira says it's luck. I say it's a genie.
Mirage Wells is real, you know. Unlike the one you saw on the way here.

locals.name: Traveller Wren
lines: Rest your feet a while. The road will still be there.
Best water for miles. I'd know, I've tried the others.
I'm only stopping a minute. I said that this morning.

people.name: Pebble
people.greeting: ...rumble. Oh! Sorry, I was napping.

people.name: Gemcutter Iolanthe
people.greeting: Every crystal has a shape hiding inside it. I just let it out.

people.name: Prospector Flint
people.greeting: Mind the Floating Stones. They float until they don't.

locals.name: Miner Greta
lines: Gem Crawlers carry the best crystal on their backs.
Ingothold's forge wants every shell they shed.
Pebble up the hill was just a boulder in my grandad's day. Then he woke up.
The tallest peak glitters at sunrise. Something's up there.

locals.name: Odile the Mapmaker
lines: Made it! The view from this page is the best in the book.
I can see Ingothold's chimneys from here.
Somebody left that chest. Not me. I only leave footprints.
Getting down is the part I never plan for.

locals.name: Polisher Mae
lines: I polish what Iolanthe cuts. My arms are very strong now.
Greta mines the rock, Flint finds the gems, and we make them shine.
A Golden Cloud rained on my crystals once. Golden rain! Very sticky.
Look closely and every crystal has a little rainbow inside.

locals.name: Apprentice Quill
lines: Iolanthe says I cut crystals like a bear cuts cake.
The Gem Crawlers eat the best crystals. We have to win them back.
Pebble up on the summit is the oldest stone on the mountain. And the chattiest.
One day I'll cut a crystal so clear you'll forget it's there.

locals.name: Wanderer Isa
lines: Pull up a log. The fire's warm and the stew is nearly edible.
I've slept under every sky in Dorlune. This one's my favourite.
Travel light, friend, and never camp downwind of a jelly.

people.name: Stardust
people.greeting: Neigh... the stars are restless tonight.

people.name: Festival-Keeper Selene
people.greeting: Welcome to Silvermoon Steps. On a full moon, the whole village climbs up to watch it rise.

people.name: Old Stargazer Bellamy
people.greeting: Lune taught me half of what I know about the stars. I taught her the other half.

locals.name: Mochi Maker Hana
lines: Moon-mochi, fresh pounded! Well. Ordinary mochi.
The Queen's mochi went missing. Everyone looks at me.
I didn't take it! I only make it. Very different.
Between us... I think the Moon Rabbits ate it themselves.

locals.name: Stargazer Lune
lines: Stardust can't fly while the skeletons roam.
Out here the stars feel close enough to pocket.
I count them every night. I'm on star nine thousand and four.
Nine thousand and five. Oh, that one's moving. That's Stardust!

locals.name: Lantern Boy Teo
lines: I hang the moon lanterns on the steps. Seventy-seven of them. I counted.
Selene says the Moon Rabbit Queen watches the festival from her hill.
Hana's mochi is the best. Don't tell her I had three.
The Shadow Apes stole the festival rice. Who steals rice?

locals.name: Night Shepherd Ottilie
lines: I shepherd at night. The sheep don't mind. They're asleep.
Bellamy's telescope can see the rabbit on the moon. Truly!
Skeletons rattle up the steps some nights. My bunny hides in my hood.
When the moon's full, the whole valley goes silver. You'll see.

locals.name: Traveller Tobin
lines: Rest your feet a while. The road will still be there.
Best water for miles. I'd know, I've tried the others.
I'm only stopping a minute. I said that this morning.

people.name: Washerwoman Wenna
people.greeting: Hold on to your hat, dear. In Thistledown the wind takes anything that isn't tied down.

people.name: Kitewright Bryn
people.greeting: A kite's only a wish with a string on it. Want to see mine?

locals.name: Courier Dot
lines: Letters for Meadowbrook! Letters for Larkspur! Letters for... smudged.
The wind took three letters today. Somewhere a goose is very well informed.
Gooey Grotto? I don't deliver there. Everything comes back sticky.
If you see a letter blowing about, it's probably mine.

locals.name: Kite-Flyer Wynn
lines: This is the windiest place in Dorlune! Perfect for kites.
I lost my red kite last week. It flew west, toward the grotto.
Something gooey and golden bounces out of there at night.
Grandma says it's the Gilded Brute, counting his treasure.

locals.name: Little Fen
lines: Wynn's my big brother. He flew a kite so high it touched a cloud!
Mum says Thistledown is the windiest place in the whole world.
I lost my hat in a gust last spring. I bet it's in Meadowbrook by now.
When I grow up I'm going to be a kite. Or a kitewright. One of those.

locals.name: Old Shepherd Tam
lines: Sheep up here grow the thickest wool. They have to, in this wind.
Wenna's washing line has been to more places than I have.
Bryn's kites can lift a lamb clean off the ground. Don't ask me how I know.
Kite Day is the best day of the year. Nobody works, and everybody runs.

locals.name: Farmer Bram
lines: Mind the pumpkins! They bruise if you look at them wrong.
The scarecrow does his best. The crows aren't impressed.
Rain, sun, slimes in the cabbages. A farmer's work is never done.

people.name: Foreman Dobbs
people.greeting: Watch your step. That puddle's not a puddle. It's a Mud Slime having a nap.

locals.name: Prospector Goldie
lines: Gold in the grotto! Real gold! ...Slimy gold.
The slimes eat coins and get shinier. I just follow them about.
Their boss calls himself the Gilded Brute. Says it's all for the Gilded King.
Never met this king. I bet he's slimy too.

locals.name: Miner Mags
lines: Dobbs says there's more gold in the goo than in the rock. He's not wrong.
Goldie weighs every nugget twice. Then she weighs it again, to be sure.
Don't swing at a Golden Slime near the cart. It gets everywhere.
Ten years I've dug this grotto, and I've never once been dry.

people.name: Confectioner Clementine
people.greeting: Welcome to Peppermint Row! Please don't lick the houses. We've had complaints.

people.name: Toffee-Puller Tibbs
people.greeting: Pull, fold, pull, fold. Toffee's all in the elbows.

locals.name: Gretel the Baker
lines: Don't nibble the houses, dear. Somebody might live in them.
I did, once. Long story. There was an oven.
These days I just bake. Gumdrops, mostly.
Wolves prowl the peaks at night. They don't like sugar. More for us.

locals.name: Hansel
lines: My sister says I eat too much. I'm just checking the mountain's still sugar.
It is. Mostly.
There's a chest at the very top of the peak. I hope it's full of fudge.
Mother Sheep's lambs came through here. The wolves took them west.

locals.name: Little Taffy
lines: Hansel and Gretel live up the hill. They know all about gingerbread houses.
Clementine lets me lick the spoon if I sweep the sprinkles.
The Candy Puffs are made of sugar, so they're always in a hurry.
This year I'm going to be crowned Gala Queen. I've practised waving.

locals.name: Sprinkle-Sweeper Lolly
lines: I sweep the sprinkles off the path every morning. They grow back every night.
Tibbs's toffee can pull a tooth out. Ask him how many he's got left.
Mind the Flame Sheep. One sneeze and the whole row smells of burnt sugar.
Every year the Gala crown gets eaten before the Gala. Every year.

locals.name: Farmer Odette
lines: Mind the pumpkins! They bruise if you look at them wrong.
The scarecrow does his best. The crows aren't impressed.
Rain, sun, slimes in the cabbages. A farmer's work is never done.

people.name: Little Red
people.greeting: Grandmother's cottage is just past the trees. Everyone says don't stray from the path. I don't. Mostly.

people.name: Grandmother Hazel
people.greeting: Come in, come in! Don't mind the wolf-shaped dent in the door.

locals.name: Bo-Peep
lines: I've lost my sheep, and I don't know where to find them.
Everyone says leave them alone and they'll come home.
Everyone hasn't met the Howlmaster.
If you climb up there... tell the lambs Bo-Peep is waiting at the bottom.

locals.name: Huntsman Corwin
lines: This is the Howlmaster's hill. Even the crows whisper here.
He keeps the stolen lambs at the top, where he can watch them.
I'm a huntsman. I don't fight wolves. I just keep an eye on them.
From very far away. Like now.

locals.name: Woodcutter Hale
lines: I chop wood by Grandmother's cottage. Handy, when a wolf drops by.
Little Red takes the long way round. She says it's prettier.
Corwin hunts the wolves and I chop the trees. Woodsend keeps us both busy.
Grandmother's door has been mended four times this year. I did all four.

locals.name: Shepherd Boy Tom
lines: Wolf! Wolf! ...Sorry. Force of habit.
Nobody believes me any more. Even when there really are wolves. Like now.
Bo-Peep lost her sheep again. I didn't do it, honest.
Grandmother Hazel gives me a muffin if I don't shout. I shout less now.

locals.name: Gravekeeper Moss
lines: Hush now. They've earned their rest.
I sweep the leaves and light the lantern. Someone should.
Every stone here has a story. Most of them end with a monster.

people.name: Nella the Tailor
people.greeting: Mind the thread! Larkspur's finest tailor, at your service.

services.name: Healer Mei
services.greeting: Welcome to Larkspur. Let me see those scrapes.

services.name: Barber Fen
services.greeting: The wind off the hills tousles everyone's hair. Let me set yours just the way you like it.

services.name: Banker Wren
services.greeting: Travelling light? Leave the rest with me. It'll be here, safe and sound, when you come back.

services.name: Larkspur Market
services.greeting: Cloth, potions and charms, fresh from the capital!

locals.name: Birdwatcher Pell
lines: Bluebirds nest on every roof in Larkspur. Bring an umbrella.
Nella the Tailor wants feathers for a dress. A swan's dress.
I told her swans don't shed for just anyone.
Swan Lake's the place. Mind the Water Slugs.

people.name: Old Swan Keeper
people.greeting: The swans come home in spring. Every one of them was once an ugly duckling.

people.name: Ferrywoman Brigid
people.greeting: Mind the gap between the boat and the jetty. And the frogs. Mostly the frogs.

people.name: Lacemaker Linnet
people.greeting: Swan Lake lace is the finest anywhere. I learned the pattern from the swans themselves.

locals.name: Odette
lines: One, two, three, turn... The swans taught me that.
By day I dance. By night... well, never mind the night.
A sorcerer's spell, they say. I say it's good exercise.
Have you seen the little grey duckling? It hides from the Water Slugs.

locals.name: Boatwright Hugo
lines: This jetty gets you halfway to the island. The other half is swimming.
There's a footbridge, mind. I just prefer my way.
The swans come home in spring. They land right... about... there.
Old Swan Keeper's fed them since he was a cygnet himself.

locals.name: Ferry Lad Corin
lines: Brigid says one day the ferry's mine. I just have to stop falling in.
The Treefrogs ride the ferry for free. I've tried charging them.
Hugo builds the boats, Brigid sails them, I bail them out.
Odette never comes over to Reedwater. She just watches from the island.

locals.name: Swan-Feeder Agatha
lines: I've fed the swans every morning for fifty years. They still hiss at me.
Linnet's lace is so fine you can read through it. I've tried.
They say the swan girl on the island was a princess once. I believe it.
Wisps drift over the water at dusk. Linnet spins their light into thread.

locals.name: Farmer Bram
lines: Mind the pumpkins! They bruise if you look at them wrong.
The scarecrow does his best. The crows aren't impressed.
Rain, sun, slimes in the cabbages. A farmer's work is never done.

people.name: Thumbelina
people.greeting: Oh! Hello, giant. Please mind the lily pads, one of them is my house.

people.name: Mayor Pipkin
people.greeting: Welcome to Lilypad Landing! Mind your feet. We're smaller than we look. Well, we look small too.

people.name: Dew-Gatherer Sorrel
people.greeting: Every morning I gather the dew from the lotus petals, before the sprites drink it all.

locals.name: Kip
lines: Shh! I'm catching a ladybug. A giant one.
They're the size of ponies here! Thumbelina rides one.
She's tiny. Thumb-tiny. Hence the name.
She wants to cross the pond to see her prince. The Lotus Sprites won't let her.

locals.name: Mister Mole
lines: I live underground, you know. Very sensible. No sun.
I asked Thumbelina to marry me. She said she'd think about it.
That was three summers ago. Still thinking, I expect.
The tunnels down there run to the Rat Cavern. Ghastly neighbours.

locals.name: Ferryman Oswin
lines: I row the little folk across on a leaf. Six at a time, if they hold on.
Pipkin's the smallest mayor in the land, and the loudest.
The Water Slugs eat the lily pads. That's like eating someone's house!
Thumbelina visits sometimes. Everyone here thinks she's very tall.

locals.name: Snail-Keeper Mopsy
lines: The tiny folk ride snails to market. I keep the snails. It's slow work.
Sorrel says a dew pearl is a morning you can keep in your pocket.
The Lantern Float is the prettiest night of the year. If it happens.
Mister Mole digs tunnels under Lilypad Landing. Nobody minds, they're cosy.

locals.name: Wanderer Pell
lines: Pull up a log. The fire's warm and the stew is nearly edible.
I've slept under every sky in Dorlune. This one's my favourite.
Travel light, friend, and never camp downwind of a jelly.

people.name: Hermit Orrin
people.greeting: The puppets on the hill used to dance for children. Now they don't stop.

people.name: Puppeteer Gianna
people.greeting: Every puppet on this hill was carved in Stringwood. Some of them just forgot to come home.

people.name: Toymender Otto
people.greeting: Bring me a broken toy and I'll mend it. Bring me a broken puppet and I'll mend it twice.

locals.name: Old Carver Beppo
lines: I carved half the puppets on this hill. Long ago.
They danced for the children at the fair. Such joy.
Then the Marionette King took up their strings, and they never stopped.
Cut his strings, friend. Set my puppets free.

locals.name: Fiddler Rook
lines: The puppets dance to my tune. Watch! ...See? Nothing.
They only dance for their king now.
I play anyway. The animals will come back when it's safe.
Hermit Orrin says they're waiting just over the hill.

locals.name: Little Mirabel
lines: This puppet's called Mister Buttons. He never ran away, he's very loyal.
Gianna puts on a show every midsummer. Last year the puppets did it themselves.
Old Beppo carved half the puppets on the hill. He misses them.
Rook plays the fiddle and the wild puppets dance. It's a bit spooky.

locals.name: Woodcarver Fenna
lines: Beetles in the wood, beetles in the shop, beetles in my lunch.
A good puppet needs good wood. A good puppeteer needs patience.
Otto mends everything. He mended my heart once. Well, my chair.
The golden strings are the magic part. Without them it's just wood.

locals.name: Traveller Wren
lines: Rest your feet a while. The road will still be there.
Best water for miles. I'd know, I've tried the others.
I'm only stopping a minute. I said that this morning.

people.name: Ambrose the Wise
people.greeting: The goddess Liora hid her treasure where only the patient look.

people.name: Smelter Bruna
people.greeting: The ore comes down the lake on rafts, and I melt it. The crabs come too. I don't melt those.

people.name: Harbourmaster Fitch
people.greeting: Rafts in, rafts out, and not one of them on time.

locals.name: Hilde the Fisher
lines: Dwarves don't fish, they say. Dwarves say a lot of things.
I caught a fish with a glowing stone in its belly once.
Ambrose said it was Dreamstone and took it off to study. I wanted it for soup.
The golems roll down to drink at dusk. Keep off the shore then.

locals.name: Scholar Wendel
lines: Ambrose sent me to count the golems. I've got as far as 'lots'.
Their cores glow like the lamps in Liora's temple.
Some say her treasure lies south, in the Hidden Steppe.
Something guards it there. Something that hits very hard.

locals.name: Raftsman Edric
lines: I pole the ore rafts down from Ingothold. Slow, but steady.
Fire Crabs love a raft. Sets the ropes smoking every time.
Bruna's forge never goes out. Not even on holidays.
Hilde catches the fish and I eat them. We're a good team.

locals.name: Little Smudge
lines: They call me Smudge because of the soot. I've washed. It doesn't help.
Fitch shouts at the rafts. The rafts don't listen.
The Golems came down from the mountain and now they won't go back.
When I'm big I'll be a smelter, like Bruna. Or a raft.

locals.name: Wanderer Isa
lines: Pull up a log. The fire's warm and the stew is nearly edible.
I've slept under every sky in Dorlune. This one's my favourite.
Travel light, friend, and never camp downwind of a jelly.

people.name: Jory
people.greeting: Rosalind fell asleep a year ago and never woke up. The whole town did.

people.name: Night-Owl Nettie
people.greeting: Can't sleep? Neither can we. Welcome to Wakewell, where nobody has yawned in a year.

people.name: Coffee-Roaster Bastian
people.greeting: Coffee? Tea? A second coffee? We've got all night. We always have all night.

locals.name: Sleepwalker Mabel
lines: Zzz... five more minutes...
Zzz... the bread's in the oven... zzz...
Mmm? Is it morning? ...No? Lovely. Zzz...
Zzz... wake Rosalind... the rock... it snores... zzz...

locals.name: Watchman Ollie
lines: I'm the night watchman. I watch the night. It's very quiet.
Everyone in Dozywick's been asleep for a year. Even the cat.
Except Jory and me. Jory's too worried. I'm too... what was I saying?
The Craghulk snores in its cave. Every snore, the whole town sighs.

locals.name: Sleepless Sid
lines: I brought a pillow from Dozywick. It doesn't work here.
Everyone over there sleeps and everyone over here can't. It's not fair.
I've counted sheep. I've counted Phantoms. I've counted counting.
Nettie says when the Craghulk stops snoring, we'll all sleep at last.

locals.name: Knitting Gran Wink
lines: I've knitted a scarf for every night I couldn't sleep. That's a lot of scarves.
My cat sleeps. Only my cat. Show-off.
Bastian's coffee could wake a stone. Not the Craghulk, sadly.
A Phantom told me a bedtime story once. It was very boring. Still didn't sleep.

locals.name: Farmer Odette
lines: Mind the pumpkins! They bruise if you look at them wrong.
The scarecrow does his best. The crows aren't impressed.
Rain, sun, slimes in the cabbages. A farmer's work is never done.

people.name: Old Ox
people.greeting: Moo... there were four of us once, and no lion dared come near.

people.name: Drum-Maker Saba
people.greeting: On the steppe, you hear a drum before you see the village. Welcome to Tallgrass.

people.name: Steppe Elder Kestrel
people.greeting: The grass grows taller than a man here, and the stories grow taller than the grass.

quests.name: The Waystone in the Tall Grass

locals.name: Herder Tamsin
lines: Steady, Brindle. It's just thunder. Probably.
Old Ox's friends wander all over the steppe now.
Four of them, tail to tail, and no lion dared come near. Now look.
If you see one, tell them the old ox misses them.

locals.name: Treasure Hunter Jasper
lines: The goddess's treasure is out here. I can smell it.
It smells like dust. Mostly dust.
There's a guardian, they say. Morvane. Hits for thousands.
I'm waiting for someone else to go first. Want to go first?

locals.name: Little Drummer Tobi
lines: Boom! Boom-boom! That's how we say hello in Tallgrass.
Saba's big drum can be heard all the way to the Old Ox. He nods along.
The Blaze Bulls set the grass on fire when they run. Then everybody runs.
Jasper says there's treasure out here. I think the treasure is the drums.

locals.name: Grass-Weaver Nan
lines: I weave the tall grass into baskets, roofs and very scratchy hats.
Tamsin's herd grazes right up to our door. Very polite cows.
Kestrel's been telling the same story for sixty years. It gets better.
When the Great Drum sounds, every herd on the steppe comes home.

locals.name: Wanderer Pell
lines: Pull up a log. The fire's warm and the stew is nearly edible.
I've slept under every sky in Dorlune. This one's my favourite.
Travel light, friend, and never camp downwind of a jelly.

people.name: Little Crab
people.greeting: Oh! Mind the persimmons, they fall hard around here.

people.name: Captain Brine
people.greeting: Ahoy! The Gull's the only ship that knows the way to Starfall Isle, and she's not ready to sail.

people.name: Pepper-Farmer Ginger
people.greeting: Bless you! Oh, you didn't sneeze? You will. Everyone does in Pepperpot Bay.

people.name: Salt-Panner Morrow
people.greeting: Salt from the sea, pepper from the hill. We season the whole coast, we do.

locals.name: Ume the Picker
lines: Achoo! Sorry. Everyone sneezes here. It's the pollen.
Little Crab grew a whole persimmon tree from one seed!
Now the apes come down from the hills to raid it.
Share the harvest, Little Crab says. The apes don't share.

locals.name: Castaway Fitz
lines: Washed up here ten years ago. Achoo! Never left.
Who'd leave? Sun, persimmons, a mountain to climb.
Somebody hid a chest at the top of the peak. Achoo!
I'd fetch it myself, but... achoo! ...the pollen's worse up there.

locals.name: Salt-Girl Perla
lines: I rake the salt pans every morning. My hair's always a bit crunchy.
Ginger's peppers are so hot the crabs sneeze fire.
Castaway Fitz says he'll leave one day. He's been saying it for ten years.
The Great Sneeze is my favourite festival. It's very loud.

locals.name: Old Sniffles Bart
lines: Achoo! Don't mind me. Achoo! It's the pepper. Achoo!
I've sneezed every day for forty years. I'm very good at it now.
The monkeys stole the peppers and now they're sneezing in the trees.
Little Crab grows persimmons, Ginger grows peppers. I grow tissues.

locals.name: Wanderer Isa
lines: Pull up a log. The fire's warm and the stew is nearly edible.
I've slept under every sky in Dorlune. This one's my favourite.
Travel light, friend, and never camp downwind of a jelly.

people.name: Temple Keeper
people.greeting: The Tidewater Shrine sank beneath the lake long ago. Something still guards it.

people.name: Ice-Carver Sigrun
people.greeting: Ice is just water that's decided to hold still. I help it decide what shape.

people.name: Soup-Wife Margery
people.greeting: Soup! Hot soup! The only thing in Icemoor that isn't frozen solid.

locals.name: Bridge Warden Aldric
lines: Halt! ...Sorry. Habit. Cross away.
I've watched this bridge since the Tidewater Shrine sank.
Some nights you can hear its bells under the ice.
The Temple Keeper says something still guards it down there.

locals.name: Ice Fisher Brin
lines: Fish bite better when it's cold. So do I.
I pulled up a bell once. A little silver one, all green with weed.
From the old shrine, says the Temple Keeper, who keeps it safe now.
Some nights the lake rings back.

locals.name: Odile the Mapmaker
lines: The island's easy to draw. Round, with a tree. Done!
The lake's harder. It freezes, then it thaws.
Briarmere's page is near the end of Liora's book.
I wonder what's on the last page. A road, I think. A green one.

locals.name: Hut-Builder Torvald
lines: I build the ice-fishing huts. In spring they float away. I build them again.
Brin catches the fish, Margery cooks them, I eat them. Teamwork.
The Frost Bears think our huts are for them. They're not.
Sigrun once carved a whole swan out of the lake. It quacked. I swear it.

locals.name: Little Ingrid
lines: This snowman's called Mister Frostbottom. He's very brave.
Aldric lets me cross the bridge if I say the password. It's 'please'.
Margery's soup is made of fish, onions and something wobbly.
On Ice Lantern Night, the whole lake glows. Like a big moon lying down.

locals.name: Traveller Tobin
lines: Rest your feet a while. The road will still be there.
Best water for miles. I'd know, I've tried the others.
I'm only stopping a minute. I said that this morning.

people.name: Shrine-Keeper Ondine
people.greeting: Pilgrims rest here before they walk the drowned halls. Rest a while too.

people.name: Innkeeper Bartholomew
people.greeting: A bed, a bowl and a bit of quiet. That's all a pilgrim needs, and all I've got.

locals.name: Diver Marisol
lines: I dive down to the old halls. Hold your breath and kick!
The jellies glow like lanterns down there.
In the deepest hall something big sleeps. It breathes in tides.
I don't go to the deepest hall.

locals.name: Pilgrim Sela
lines: I walk the shrine's halls every day, as my teachers did.
The water rose long ago. We kept walking.
The Wavecrest Dragon was a guardian once. Now it guards only its anger.
Be gentle with it, if you can.

locals.name: Weary Pilgrim Anwen
lines: I walked here from Meadowbrook. My feet have opinions about it.
Sela walks the drowned halls every day. I walked them once. Once was enough.
Bartholomew's stew is the best thing about the pilgrimage. Don't tell Ondine.
They say if you listen at the shrine steps, the sea sings back.

locals.name: Bell-Polisher Ruth
lines: I polish the shrine bells. The sea air turns them green overnight.
Marisol dives for the old offerings. She brings me the bells.
The Gem Crawlers pick the pearls out of the walls. Little thieves.
Ondine says the Wavecrest Dragon guards the deepest hall. I'll stay up here.

locals.name: Traveller Wren
lines: Rest your feet a while. The road will still be there.
Best water for miles. I'd know, I've tried the others.
I'm only stopping a minute. I said that this morning.

people.name: Spinner Arachne
people.greeting: Hush. Listen. Every thread in this hollow whispers, if you're quiet enough.

locals.name: Bard Lyle
lines: Hello? ...hello? ...hello?
Oh! A real person. I thought you were another echo.
The hollow whispers. Mostly about the Silver Wraith.
The Warden holds the only way through to the Emerald Road. Few get past.

locals.name: Silk-Winder Nita
lines: I wind Arachne's silk onto spools. It hums when you wind it.
Lyle sings to the echoes. The echoes sing back, slightly worse.
Crystal Widow silk is stronger than steel and softer than a cloud.
The Silverfang Warden lives deeper down. We don't wind silk down there.

people.name: Emerald Guard
people.greeting: Follow the road to the Emerald City. Nobody said it was safe.

quests.name: At the End of the Road

people.name: Spectacle-Maker Fennimore
people.greeting: Everyone who goes through the gate wears green spectacles. Who do you think makes them?

people.name: Poppy-Farmer Dell
people.greeting: Mind the poppies. They make you sleepy. I've been yawning since I was four.

locals.name: Tin Woodman
lines: Oil can... oil can...
Ah, that's better. I've stood here rusting since the dragon came.
I'm walking to the Emerald City. For a heart.
The dragon at the gate won't let anyone by. Not even a polite tin man.

locals.name: Odile the Mapmaker
lines: The last page! Or nearly. The Emerald City is just past the dragon.
I've drawn every page of Liora's book. All but one.
I'll draw the city when someone clears the way.
No rush. I'm very good at waiting, and very bad at dragons.

locals.name: Poppy-Picker Sam
lines: Zzz... oh! I'm awake. I'm picking. I'm definitely picking.
Dell says if you pick poppies too long you fall asleep in the field. Zzz...
The Tin Woodman stood by the road so long a bird nested in his hat.
The Emerald City is just past the dragon. Nobody's been in for years.

locals.name: Green-Glass Grandpa Hux
lines: Through green glass, everything looks like emeralds. Even porridge.
Fennimore polishes a thousand lenses a year. His eyes are very tired.
Odile drew my picture for her book. She made me taller. Good girl.
Golden Clouds drift over the road and rain little drops of gold. Sticky.

locals.name: Traveller Tobin
lines: Rest your feet a while. The road will still be there.
Best water for miles. I'd know, I've tried the others.
I'm only stopping a minute. I said that this morning.

people.name: Mother Lumen
people.greeting: Welcome to Glimmerbough, traveller. Mind your head: our doors are small, but our welcome isn't.

people.name: Pip the Lamplighter
people.greeting: Psst, down here! I'm Pip. I light Glimmerbough's lanterns, when the moths leave me any light.

services.name: Dewdrop
services.greeting: Rest a while under the leaves, dear. Starlight mends whatever it touches.

services.name: Thistle
services.greeting: Potions, seals and feathers! Everything a traveller far from home could need.

services.name: Clover
services.greeting: Far from home, and carrying too much? Leave it with me, under the roots. Nothing gets lost here.

locals.name: Stargazer Lune
lines: A star fell here long ago. The island still hums with it.
The crystals grow wherever its light landed. Don't lick them. I did.
At night the stones sing along with the sky. Listen.
The wisps are sparks of the fallen star, looking for the way home.

locals.name: Captain Marlow
lines: Back to Sneezle Sands? She's ready when you are. Just walk aboard.
Forty years at sea, and this island still gives me goosebumps.
The stars steer us here. Mostly. Sometimes it's the gulls.
Mind the gangplank. It squeaks, but it holds.

locals.name: Bramble the Gardener
lines: The houses here grow, you know. We just ask the trees nicely.
Glimmerbough grew up round the crystals the star left behind.
If a door looks too small, knock anyway. We'll come out to you.
Some nights the hill glows brighter than the moon. That's the star, dreaming.

locals.name: Little Wren
lines: Are you a giant? Mother Lumen says giants are just people who ate their greens.
One day I'll catch a Starmoth and ride it all the way to the moon.
Pip says the star on the hill is lonely. I'd be lonely too, so far from home.
Shh! If you're very quiet, the lanterns hum.
North of here there's a cave where the crystals sing. I'm too little to go.

locals.name: Traveller Wren
lines: Rest your feet a while. The road will still be there.
Best water for miles. I'd know, I've tried the others.
I'm only stopping a minute. I said that this morning.

locals.name: Crystal-Singer Opaline
lines: Hush. Hear that? The crystals sing for anyone who stops to listen.
I came down to learn their song. Forty years on, I know the chorus.
The deeper you go, the brighter it gets. That's the Prism Drake.
Geodes float because they're full of light. Crack one and it glows.

quests.title: Hope of Meadowbrook
quests.description: Elder Oak gives every new adventurer three gifts: a wooden sword, a novice ring and a pet egg. Hatch your egg from the Bag, then come back to me.

question.text: Before you go, tell me: what do you treasure most?

quests.title: Jelly Trouble
quests.description: Jelly Puffs keep sliming our vegetable patch! Head east to Sunny Meadow and defeat 3 of them.

quests.title: A New Friend
quests.description: Every adventurer needs friends. Take these Seal Stones and throw one at a monster with Capture: the weaker it is, the better your odds. Each throw uses a stone up, and it may take a few tries!

quests.title: Wish Upon a Star
quests.description: Long ago a star fell by Meadowbrook's well, and its light still sleeps in a Wishing Seal: a stone that never fails. Befriend three more monsters, show me you'll be kind to them, and it's yours.

quests.title: Choose Your Path
quests.description: Reach level 10, then speak to a guild master in town to choose your path: Fighter, Mage or Beast Tamer.

quests.title: Pineapple Harvest
quests.description: Pineapple Sprouts have taken over Pineapple Shore, south of Meadowbrook. Defeat 5.

quests.title: The Bouncy Menace
quests.description: Something bounces in the dark of Twilight Woods, east of Sunny Meadow. Defeat 3 Bouncy Buns.

quests.title: Swamp Song
quests.description: Frogs croak all night south of Sunny Meadow and nobody can sleep! Quiet 4 Treefrogs in Frog Swamp.

quests.title: Monkey Business
quests.description: Wood Monkeys from the Smiling Forest, east of Gumdrop Peaks, keep stealing our apples. Defeat 5.

quests.title: Sheep Shearing
quests.description: The Flame Sheep of the Smiling Forest have set the market awnings alight again. Defeat 4, please!

quests.title: Lights in the Valley
quests.description: Strange lights drift through Shiverdell, south of Twilight Woods. Defeat 4 Wisps and see what's there.

quests.title: The Rat King
quests.description: The dwarves of Ingothold are cut off! A Rat King has taken over the cavern east of Shiverdell. Defeat him.

quests.title: Dragon Hangover
quests.description: A dragon's been drinking at the oasis in Genie Desert, east of town, and scaring off the caravans. Sober him up… with force.

unlocks.name: Who's Afraid of the Big Bad Wolf?

quests.title: Crystal Hearts
quests.description: We need Gem Crawler shells for the forge. Defeat 4 on Crystal Mountain, south of Ingothold.

quests.title: Who's Afraid of the Big Bad Wolf?
quests.description: A Big Bad Wolf prowls the Snow White Forest, east of the Smiling Forest, and no one dares take the road north to Moonwhisper. Be brave, and be careful.

quests.title: Lost Little Lambs
quests.description: Baa! Golden Hamsters keep stuffing their cheeks with the clover my little lambs need. Shoo away 3 of them and my lambs can graze again.

quests.title: Shell Snatchers
quests.description: Click-clack! Those Mud Eagles swoop down and snatch the prettiest shells off my beach. Chase off 3 of them for an old crab, will you?

quests.title: Straw, Sticks and Bricks
quests.description: My brothers built houses of straw and sticks, and now Tree Snakes keep coiling round them! Chase off 5 Tree Snakes so we can finish the house of bricks before the wolf comes.

quests.title: Moonlight Thieves
quests.description: The Shade Puffs are drinking up the moonlight, and without it I fade away. Pop 4 Shade Puffs and let the light come back to Twilight Woods.

quests.title: The Frog Prince
quests.description: A kiss? Goodness, no. What I need is my golden ball back from the pond, and the Water Slugs are guarding it. Defeat 4 Water Slugs and a prince's reward is yours.

quests.title: The Ugly Duckling
quests.description: The Mud Slimes splash mud on my feathers and laugh at me. Would you make them stop? Defeat 4 Mud Slimes. One day I'll be a swan, you'll see!

quests.title: The Lion and the Mouse
quests.description: An Earth Lion once spared my life, so now I look out for him. The Blaze Bulls keep stampeding through his den! Defeat 3 Blaze Bulls and we'll both owe you one.

quests.title: Puss in Boots
quests.description: My master the Marquis needs a clear road to his castle, but Black Widows keep spinning webs across it. Clear away 4 Black Widows and I'll tip my hat to you.

quests.title: Stormy Crystals
quests.description: Golden Clouds keep raining on my crystals until they go dull. Chase off 4 Golden Clouds so the mountain can sparkle again.

quests.title: Bear Hugs
quests.description: The Frost Bears keep hugging my snowman friends, and a Frost Bear hug squeezes a snowman flat. Defeat 3 Frost Bears before there's nobody left but snowdrifts!

quests.title: Stardust's Night Flight
quests.description: I can't fly under the moon while Poison Skeletons haunt Moonwhisper. Defeat 4 of them and I'll carry your name across the stars.

quests.title: The Gilded Brute
quests.description: Gooey Grotto, west of the Windswept Downs, is full of Golden Slimes. Their master calls himself the Gilded Brute. Defeat him.

quests.title: The Wandering Flock
quests.description: The wolves of Gumdrop Peaks took Mother Sheep's lambs to the Big Bad Wolf's Lair, west of the mountain. Thin out their pack: defeat 6 Earth Wolves.

quests.title: The Howlmaster
quests.description: The pack still follows its leader. Find the Howlmaster deep in the lair and bring those lambs home.

quests.title: Soft as a Cloud
quests.description: I need wool for a very special dress, the kind a swan would wear. Candy Puffs spin the softest fluff; bring me what 8 of them leave behind.

quests.title: An Ugly Duckling's Wish
quests.description: The little grey duckling of Swan Lake hides from the Water Slugs. Clear 6 of them so it can swim out and meet the swans.

quests.title: A Little Kindness
quests.description: The Lotus Sprites won't let me cross the pond to see my prince. Would you shoo away 6 of them? Gently, please.

quests.title: A Place to Belong
quests.description: The Wooden Puppets chased every animal off Marionette Rise. Break 8 of them and the animals can come home.

quests.title: The Marionette King
quests.description: The puppets dance for their king at the top of the hill. Cut his strings for good.

quests.title: Mystery of the Dreamstone
quests.description: Dreamstone Golems roll about Ingothold Lake. Their cores glow like the goddess Liora's treasure. Defeat 6 and let me study one.

quests.title: Treasures of Goddess Liora
quests.description: The ore points south, to the Hidden Steppe. Morvane guards the goddess's treasure there, and can hit for thousands. Bring a strong party.

quests.title: Sleeping Rosalind
quests.description: The Dream Phantoms keep Dozywick dreaming. Defeat 8 of them, then wake Rosalind by beating the Craghulk that snores in the cave.

quests.title: The Craghulk
quests.description: Now the monster itself. It's big, it's stone, and it has been asleep for a year. Wake it up the hard way.

quests.title: No More Nightmares
